title: Scenario Simulator — Runtime Contract
description: The one runtime shape the shared ladder engine (js/sim-player.js) drives. Every scenario type normalizes into this shape via type.toRuntime(source). This schema is the SUPERSET: the common core is required; additive blocks (cast, state, canon, coverage/hazards/decoys/scene) appear only on the types that need them. Companion reference: scenario-simulator-json-contract.html. NOTE: this describes the RUNTIME object, not the authored source the Studio exports and not the compiled system-prompt string (type.compile → string). Fields the engine actually reads carry x-engine-reads:true — everything else is prompt fuel or render-surface data.
x-source-of-truth: Verified against toRuntime(DEFAULT) dumps for mix-arc, branching-arc, ensemble-arc, scene-sweep, and guided-arc (recipe → mix-arc) on 2026-08-05.

title.description: Scenario name — shown in the learner top bar and results screen.

course.description: The training/course this scenario lives inside (register cue for the prompt).

characterName.description: The first/primary counterpart label. Per-phase counterpart overrides it. Absent on scene-sweep.

framing.description: One-line premise; opens the compiled system prompt.

learnerRole.description: Who the learner plays across every phase.

establishing.description: Cold-open framing block shown before the scenario begins.

playbook.description: Optional reference points surfaced to the learner/coach.

phases.description: THE LADDER. The app indexes this by state.phaseIdx and is the sole source of truth for which rung is live. Produced by toRuntime(): branching/ensemble/scene-sweep author phases[] directly; mix-arc (and guided-arc via toMixArc) derive them from beats[].

opening.description: Seeded reflection warm-up bubble(s). MAY be empty ([]) — when reflection is off (e.g. ensemble Bullying default) the player boots straight into phase 1.

sceneLineCaption.description: Byline for the learner's own scene lines. Always 'You' in current builds.

state.description: ADDITIVE (mix · branching · ensemble · guided). Session variables surfaced on the per-turn [SYSTEM STATE] line and written by phase transitions[].set.

cast.description: ADDITIVE (branching · ensemble). Character behavior models. One entry for branching; many for ensemble (each phase names its own counterpart). Read by compile() into the prompt — NOT by the engine.

canon.description: ADDITIVE (branching · ensemble). Continuity facts the prompt must keep consistent across phases.

hazards.description: ADDITIVE (scene-sweep only). The real observable hazards, with hotspot geometry and fix/prevent follow-ups.

decoys.description: ADDITIVE (scene-sweep only). Plausible-but-safe items, separate from hazards so coverage/spotted never counts them.

scene.description: ADDITIVE (scene-sweep only). The observed image + its authored descriptions.

Phase.description: One rung of the ladder. Three authored flavors collapse here: a lean ladder phase (branching/ensemble), a rich beat phase (mix/guided — adds type/character/media/hasRightAnswer/throughLine), and a perception phase (scene-sweep — uses kind + flat signpost/prompt that toRuntime folds into entry).

id.description: Unique phase id. transitions[].next references it; the app cues delivery by it.

level.description: Human progress label, e.g. 'Level 1 · early warning signs'.

world.description: Interaction mode. 'scene' flips the learner's input to the character and enters scene mode; 'coaching' faces the coach. Present on mix/branching/ensemble/guided phases; scene-sweep uses `kind` instead.

kind.description: scene-sweep only. Selects the optional render surface via ctx.outcomeBlock/coverageBlock (self-guarding hook). A 'spot' phase mounts the perception canvas; no hook → no surface code runs.

counterpart.description: Who the learner faces in a scene. A name (e.g. 'Ray'), '' for coaching, or 'Narrator' for a narrated scene with no speaking counterpart.

maxTurns.description: Learner-turn cap for the phase. At the cap the app forces the model to resolve and report a tier — the phase cannot run long. The app owns advancement, not the model.

entry.description: The LOCKED, app-authored open of the phase, appended by applyDeliver().

inputPlaceholder.description: Placeholder for the learner's input box in this phase.

exitCriteria.description: What 'done' means; drives the coach's probing and the tier it reports. Prompt-only.

reactionGuidance.description: How the counterpart/coach should react. Prompt-only.

calibration.description: Tier vocabulary the model may report for this phase. Read by compile() into the prompt; the reported tier drives transitions[].

transitions.description: On phase close, the recorded tier selects a transition → the next phase and any session-state writes.

type.description: mix-arc/guided authoring type; toRuntime derives `world` from it (roleplay → scene, else coaching).

character.description: mix-arc roleplay beat: the counterpart model. Prompt-only.

hasRightAnswer.description: mix/guided coaching beat: whether there is a correct read to land.

throughLine.description: mix/guided: the point the coach must land.

signpost.description: scene-sweep authored field; toRuntime copies it into entry.signpost.

prompt.description: scene-sweep authored field; toRuntime copies it into entry.prompt.

Entry.description: The locked opener of a phase. entryBeatsFor() reads these in order: tier-selected bridge, signpost, stimulus cards (from phase.media), prompt, scripted beats.

bridge.description: Fallback opener when no per-tier bridge matches.

bridgesByTier.description: Map of prior-phase tier → the bridge line that opens this phase. bridgesByTier[prevTier] wins over `bridge`.

signpost.description: The coach's framing line for the phase.

prompt.description: The task/question posed to the learner (coaching phases).

beats.description: Scripted scene open — narration + dialogue delivered verbatim when a scene phase begins.

cta.description: Button label to enter/advance the phase, e.g. 'Step into the room'.

Beat.description: One scripted line. Rendered purely by speaker + kind — never by inspecting text.

Transition.description: A tier-routed edge out of a phase. closePhase() picks the transition whose onTier matches the recorded tier (or the first onTier-less transition as default), writes `set` into session state, and routes to `next`.

onTier.description: Tier this edge fires on. '' = the default/fallback edge.

next.description: Target phase id. Blank/omitted = the next phase in order; a target that resolves out of range terminates the ladder.

set.description: Session-state writes applied on close: { stateVarKey: newValue }. Only keys already declared in scenario.state are written.

tier.description: Tier label the model may report, e.g. 'STRONG', 'NEUTRAL', 'UNTHOUGHTFUL'.

guidance.description: How the coach should read and respond to this tier.

talkItThrough.description: The VERBATIM teach-opener. When the model's turn begins with this line, runArcEngine() knows the phase is closing (teachOpener detection).

points.description: The debrief content the coach lands. Prompt-only.

Character.description: A single counterpart behavior model (mix-arc roleplay beat). Prompt-only.

CastMember.description: A first-class character model (branching = one; ensemble = many). Prompt-only. Ensemble adds disclosures[] (earned reveals).

baseline.description: Default demeanor before the learner acts.

disclosures.description: ensemble only. Facts the character reveals only when the learner earns them.

Reaction.description: A when/then behavior rule for a character.

earnedBy.description: The learner behavior that unlocks it.

Media.description: Observe-beat stimulus (mix-arc). Its segments become locked stimulus cards in entryBeatsFor().

MediaSegment.description: One stimulus card. x-engine-reads: entryBeatsFor() renders a clip card (video src) or a message card (kind:'message').

src.description: Video source. Empty → the described moment is shown as a caption card instead.

kind.description: 'message' → renders as a forwarded-message card; otherwise a clip card.

StateVar.description: A declared session variable. Its live value is surfaced on the [SYSTEM STATE] line and written by transitions[].set.

key.description: Identifier written by transitions and read on the state line.

label.description: Human label shown on the state line.

Coverage.description: scene-sweep coverage target: how many observable hazards count as 'enough'.

total.description: Count of real hazards in the scene.

required.description: How many must be spotted to pass the Observe beat.

short.description: Short label for the coverage rail.

zone.description: Where it is, in plain language, for coach nudges.

full.description: Full explanation of why it's a hazard.

synonyms.description: Comma-separated learner phrasings that count as spotting it.

source.description: Provenance / citation, e.g. a course object id.

Decoy.description: A plausible-but-safe item (scene-sweep). Never counts toward coverage.

note.description: Why it's actually fine — the coach's response if the learner flags it.

Spot.description: Hotspot geometry. Points are a polygon in normalized 0–1 coords against the DRAWN image (object-fit: contain, letterbox-aware). Shared by the live tap-to-mark and the Studio place-the-hotspot editor (window.SceneSweepGeo).

points.description: Polygon vertices as [x, y] pairs, each in [0,1].

canonDescription.description: Authoritative description the coach grounds on.

type.description: How the opening context is delivered.

text.description: The narration/read-along script AND the coach's picture of the setup.

sound.description: Whether the cold-open clip plays with its own audio (vs muted + captions).

Reflection.description: The opening warm-up. When enabled with a prompt, its text becomes scenario.opening; the model calibrates (no tier) before phase 1.

enabled.description: false → no warm-up; scenario.opening is [] and the player boots into phase 1.
